headline: Last session: Sensex slipped into red while Nifty gained 75 points; smallcaps showed resilience amid global volatility.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 21 September.

why: Sensex slipped into the red territory following late-session profit booking.
Nifty 50 managed to close with a gain of 75 points despite broader market pressure.
Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities weighed on sentiment.
Concerns over crude oil price volatility and FII outflows kept investors cautious.
whatHappening: Public sector bank chiefs are meeting the Finance Ministry to manage an upcoming three-day strike.
The government has issued warnings regarding cyberattacks targeting the emerging semiconductor ecosystem.
Investors are monitoring potential geopolitical shifts as Iran threatens to exit the nuclear treaty.
Market participants are preparing for the new trading week with a focus on support levels for Nifty.

summary: The Indian market showed mixed results in the last session, with the Nifty gaining 75 points while the Sensex slipped into the red. Investors are closely monitoring the upcoming three-day strike by public sector banks and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Focus remains on the semiconductor ecosystem and crude oil prices as the market prepares for the new trading week.
